184: One Apply, two tracks. The booking track is the employer's — it is about a calendar slot, and it ends when the interview is held. The pipeline track is the agency's — it is about the hiring decision, and it runs for weeks. They describe the same person but share no status field, which is why a candidate can sit in Screening without holding an interview slot, and why an interview can be booked with no pipeline card behind it. Everything an admin does is a gate on the top band, before an applicant ever sees a job.
186: How a live job fair runs
187:
The third product, and the one that looks deceptively like a calendar. On event day
    the constraint is physical: a company has a fixed number of interviewers, each interview
    takes a fixed time, and two applicants cannot sit in the same chair. Everything below
    exists to keep that constraint true while hundreds of people book at once.
188: Capacity — what actually exists to book
194: Two directions — matching runs both ways
205: The seat, not the calendar entry, is the scarce thing. Both directions funnel into a single claim that runs inside one database transaction. SKIP LOCKED is the Postgres job-queue pattern: when two people accept the same time in the same instant they lock different interviewer rows and both succeed against different seats — rather than one erroring, or worse, both being told a seat is free that isn't. It also means nobody is ever told "full" while a seat is genuinely available, which is the failure a naïve count()-then-insert produces under load.

1110: /dashboard/billing — one paid invoice with a credit note, one outstanding
1113: Invoices are INV-YYYY-NNNN, credit notes CN-YYYY-NNNN — separate sequences, no silent gaps. An accountant reads a gap as a missing document.
1115: A placement's fee can be billed exactly once — the database itself refuses a duplicate. Voiding an invoice frees the fee to be re-raised on a correction.
1117: A paid invoice cannot be voided or edited. The correction is a credit note: its own numbered document both sides can reconcile, with tax at the invoice's rate, so it reverses what was actually charged.
1119: The outstanding figure subtracts credit notes — a fully credited invoice is not money anyone is waiting for.
1121: A client can carry an agreed rate — e.g. 1.2 months of salary, the Taiwan convention. A new placement takes its fee from the rate only when no explicit fee was agreed; a blank fee stays blank rather than looking computed.
